topics.label: Introduction to the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing the learning outcomes and outlining the progressive hallmark framework of tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and oncogenic mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations deregulate signaling cascades such as Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinases to sustain cellular proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Differentiation blocks in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how impaired cellular differentiation contributes to malignancy in hematopoietic leukemias and intestinal carcinomas.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptotic cell death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells avoid programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and dysregulation of Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore telomere maintenance, senescence bypass mechanisms, p53 stress integration, and provide a concluding overview of cell-autonomous growth hallmarks.

topics.label: Cancer metabolism and metabolic reprogramming
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze altered cancer energetics, including the Warburg effect, tissue-of-origin metabolic adaptations, and the oncogenic role of Krebs cycle mutations and oncometabolites.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis and vascular recruitment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch required by developing tumors to recruit blood supply for nutrient and oxygen delivery.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genetics of metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the dissemination cascade of tumor cells, the use of liquid biopsies for longitudinal tracking, the seed-and-soil model, and genomic findings in metastatic lesions.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing for the lecture, summarizing the hallmark paradigm and providing closing remarks.
